licences.author: Kurt Soldan (1891–1946), piano reduction
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the No. 31 Finale (671 bars) read in fourteen page ranges, sung lines and piano each by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the zoomed page by a judge, a separate sweep for dynamics and other marks, then checked bar by bar by eight fresh proofreaders (one fix in this section: the right-hand E♭ tied from bar 3 into bar 4). The German singing translation is left out. All the singers of this section have a staff throughout, with rests where the print leaves a staff out; singers who do not sing in this section are left out. Cut from the one-file finale at bars 173–204: from the Larghetto (3/4) to the first bar of the Allegro (bar 204 of the finale), because the sisters' and Ferrando's “cor” and Guglielmo's “-nor” fall on its first beat as they drink; that bar also opens “Miei signori, tutto è fatto”. A slur printed in bars 3–4 between the two voices of the right hand is not encoded. Playback tempo ♩ = 50 for the Larghetto, the last bar at the Allegro's ♩ = 186, from René Jacobs's recording (harmonia mundi), whose track for this canon and the notary scene lasts 3:43 (this section about 2 minutes).
